exposure: number of prior cesarean deliveries (one or two)
outcome: composite maternal morbidity (chorioamnionitis, transfusion, hysterectomy, uterine rupture, ICU admission)
composite neonatal morbidity (5-minute Apgar score <3, assisted ventilation, NICU admission, surfactant/antibiotic use, seizures)
cohort: Pregnant individuals with live births in the United States between 2014 and 2021, including those with twin or singleton pregnancies and one or two prior cesarean deliveries, and their neonates.
finding: No significant differences in composite maternal or neonatal morbidity were found among twin pregnancies based on the number of prior cesarean deliveries or mode of planned delivery, although VBAC rates varied significantly across groups.
mod_finding: The VBAC rate for twin pregnancies with two prior cesarean deliveries undergoing TOLAC was 37.8%, significantly lower than for those with one prior cesarean delivery (61.5%) or singleton pregnancies with two prior cesarean deliveries (58.0%).
cross-section timing: Data collected from live births between 2014 and 2021.
